executive_insights.title: Documentation Maturity Masks Commercial Credential Friction
executive_insights.summary: 17 applications with Large, well-documented APIs still gate production credentials behind paid plans, mandatory app/KYB reviews, or enterprise contracts — including DealCloud, Pylon, Lark, Google Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn Ads. Across all 100 apps, 27% require paid plans, admin/app approval, or sales/enterprise gating despite 98% having public APIs.
executive_insights.business_implication: Separate technical schema generation from credential-provisioning UX: invest in managed OAuth apps, pre-approved partner reviews (Google Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Amazon SP-API), and BYO-credential flows for enterprise tenants.

executive_insights.title: First-Party MCP Adoption Has Crossed the Tipping Point — Shifting Composio's Moat to Auth & Parity
executive_insights.summary: 81 platforms ship official first-party MCP servers and 2 ship vendor-supported sample/beta MCPs (Twilio, Amazon SP-API), while Composio has verified dedicated toolkits for 79/100 (79%). Many vendor MCPs remain read-only, beta-gated, or lack Dynamic Client Registration (Help Scout, Aircall, DealCloud, Front, Copper).
executive_insights.business_implication: Wrapping raw endpoints is no longer a durable moat. Composio's differentiation lies in unified multi-tenant OAuth/token lifecycle management, full write-action parity where vendor MCPs are read-only, and cross-app session orchestration.

executive_insights.title: OAuth 2.0 Dominates Multi-Tenant Readiness, While Dual-Auth Splits Dev vs. Production
executive_insights.summary: 77 apps support OAuth 2.0 and 62 support API keys, with 41 offering both. Category auth patterns diverge sharply: Developer/Infra and Productivity combine OAuth + PATs for self-service onboarding, whereas Ad Networks enforce strict OAuth-only multi-stage review.
executive_insights.business_implication: Standardizing OAuth 2.0 + PKCE with automatic token refresh and regional domain routing (Zoho, Datadog, Pylon, Smartsheet) unlocks the largest addressable integration footprint with minimal per-app auth engineering.

executive_insights.title: Category Readiness Bifurcates Sharply Between Developer/Productivity and Fintech/AI-Native
executive_insights.metric: Support and Helpdesk (8/10 Ready) vs. Finance and Fintech (1/10 Ready)
executive_insights.summary: Support and Helpdesk leads with 8/10 apps Ready to build and 2/10 offering Free self-service credentials, whereas Finance and Fintech has only 1/10 Ready to build due to KYB underwriting, enterprise gating, or non-standard surfaces.
executive_insights.business_implication: Prioritize rapid toolkit expansion in high-velocity self-service categories (Dev/Infra, Productivity, Support, SEO/Scraping) while assigning dedicated partner-engineering pods to Fintech and Ad-Tech verticals.

executive_insights.title: 6 High-Readiness 'White-Space' Quick Wins Lack Dedicated Composio Toolkits
executive_insights.summary: Out of 53 Ready-to-build apps with Medium/Large APIs and Free/Trial access, 6 do not yet have a verified dedicated Composio toolkit: Front, LiveAgent, Vonage, WooCommerce, SE Ranking, Reducto. All have mature public APIs and clear documentation.
executive_insights.business_implication: Shipping these white-space toolkits first delivers the fastest ROI per engineering week, immediately closing catalog gaps in Support (Front, LiveAgent), Communications (Vonage), Ecommerce (WooCommerce), SEO (SE Ranking), and AI Document Parsing (Reducto).

accuracy_metrics.evaluation_denominator_definition: 20 stratified apps (2 per category across all 10 categories) x 7 core fields (auth_methods, credential_acquisition, api_availability, api_breadth, mcp_status, composio_integration, buildability) = 140 evaluated fields. Strict rule: only 'Correct' counts toward accuracy; 'Partially correct', 'Incorrect', and 'Unresolved'/'Unknown' fields count as 0 correct.
